Q134290371.summary: Christ sits enthroned within a pointed mandorla, blessing with his right hand and holding a book, at the centre of a tall ivory panel. Around him the four evangelists sit at their desks writing, each accompanied by his winged symbol in a roundel, while the vertical and horizontal bands are inscribed LUX, LEX, REX and PAX: light, law, king and peace. The plaque, probably made for a Gospel book cover, presents Christ as the source of the four Gospels.
facts: The museum label (as recorded in the photograph's title) attributes the plaque to Cologne, 960–980.
The four words on the cross-shaped bands, LUX, LEX, REX and PAX, are carved directly on the plaque and frame the mandorla on all four sides.
Q134290371.notes: Inv. Kg 54:209. Title was only an inventory label. Details rest on the museum label as transcribed in the Commons filename; no online museum record was found.

Q116245184.summary: This slender ivory leaf, once the wing of a small Byzantine triptych, carries three scenes stacked one above another. At the top the Virgin of the Annunciation stands before an architectural backdrop; in the centre Christ hangs on the cross with a mourner beside him; and at the bottom the angel sits upon the empty tomb, announcing the Resurrection. Read from top to bottom, the little panel traces the whole arc of salvation, from the Incarnation to Easter morning.
facts: The Met describes the panel as a fragmentary door whose interior shows the Virgin of the Annunciation, the Crucifixion and the angel seated on Christ's tomb.
It is a small object, only about 19.3 cm high and 4.6 cm wide, and is dated 970–1030; it was probably carved in Constantinople.
